lines.trans: Oh, good morning, Chef!
Mikhail will give us a restroom as we ask.
Chef, I only need a tiny moment in there.
Please, do not worry.
Right now we will fix everything quickly.
What is going on there, did the elevator break?
No, Mikhail, there is a little problem there.
I am checking whether everything is ready for the opening.
Would you not like to join us?
We will lose all our guests like this!
If you want to keep them, stay out of my way!
Goodness, why are you acting like children?
Cannot reach an agreement? Toss a coin.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I am with you.
My butterfly.
Take more air in.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'брый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good').

examples.trans: Welcome to our hotel!
Good morning, Timur.
Oh, good morning, Chef!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'morning' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: They were still having breakfast this morning.
Good morning, Timur.
Oh, good morning, Chef!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.trans: Please make coffee for the tables.

examples.text: Михаил сделает нам туалет, как просим.
examples.trans: Mikhail will give us a restroom as we ask.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером я сделаю ей предложение!
examples.trans: Tonight I will propose to her!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We are almost there already.
We work better than everyone here.

examples.text: Сейчас мы быстро наведём здесь порядок!
examples.trans: Right now we will quickly restore order here!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'restroom' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have been asking for a restroom for two months.
A restroom must be earned first.

examples.text: Михаил сделает нам туалет, как просим.
examples.trans: Mikhail will give us a restroom as we ask.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Он ведёт себя как ревнивый парень.
examples.trans: He behaves like a jealous boyfriend.

examples.text: Я как будто в театр сходил.
examples.trans: It is as if I went to the theater.
And how should I react?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'invite/ask', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.trans: You yourselves asked for five kilograms.
We asked for only five individual ones.

examples.text: Михаил сделает нам туалет, как просим.
examples.trans: Mikhail will give us a restroom as we ask.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I am with you.
My butterfly.
Take more air in.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What are you doing in there right now?

examples.text: Надеюсь, шеф ничего там не сломает.
examples.trans: I hope the chef does not break anything up there.

examples.text: Там же ставки. Хотите в долю?
examples.trans: There are bets there. Do you want a cut?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').

examples.trans: We have become completely absent-minded.
I must not get nervous right now at all.
Chef, I only need a tiny moment in there.

meanings.en: a little bit, just a little
meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'a tiny bit', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I only need a tiny moment in there.

examples.text: Нам нужно чуть-чуть потерпеть и немножко поработать.
examples.trans: We need to be patient a little and work a bit.
Wait just a little bit longer.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

examples.trans: Please make coffee for the tables.
Please, do not worry.
A coffee, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I must not get nervous right now at all.
I have no idea.
No, nothing.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'лноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'worry'.

examples.trans: Don't worry.
I'm nervous.
Don't worry, I won't.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: I must not get nervous right now at all.
And right now excuse me.
Listen, tell me right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Come on, everything is fine.
Come on, that is all.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Сейчас мы быстро наведём здесь порядок!
examples.trans: Right now we will quickly restore order here!

examples.text: Быстро уберите всех тараканов с кухни!
examples.trans: Quickly remove all the cockroaches from the kitchen!
Right now we will fix everything quickly.

meanings.en: to fix, to correct, to put right
meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'править'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'we will fix', paired with 'исправлять'.

examples.trans: Right now we will fix everything quickly.
Excuse us, we will fix everything.

examples.text: Ученик быстро исправил ошибку в тетради.
examples.trans: The pupil quickly corrected the mistake in his notebook.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is with you, mommy, huh?
Did something happen?
What kind of nonsense is this?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'elevator' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: What is going on there, did the elevator break?

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть лифт.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always elevator.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ломаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'broke down', paired with 'ломаться'.

examples.trans: My tank broke.
Yesterday the washing machine broke down.
This stupid machine simply broke.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No, nothing.
No more bets.
Is it normal to be jealous, or not?

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'большой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('small').

examples.trans: No, Mikhail, there is a little problem there.

examples.text: Это небольшой комплимент от нашего заведения.
examples.trans: This is a small gift from our establishment.

examples.text: Мы живём в небольшом тихом городе.
examples.trans: We live in a small, quiet town.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'блемка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'little problem' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: No, Mikhail, there is a little problem there.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть проблемка.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always little problem.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to check, test, verify', paired with 'проверить'.

examples.text: Я проверяю, всё ли готово к открытию.
examples.trans: I am checking whether everything is ready for the opening.
Hand it here, check the order.
He is testing us.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'whether', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We have become completely absent-minded.
How did you spend this night?
Oh, I see that you received it.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ready').

examples.text: Я проверяю, всё ли готово к открытию.
examples.trans: I am checking whether everything is ready for the opening.
And everyone get ready now.

examples.text: Я хочу, чтобы ты приготовил пиццу.
examples.trans: I want you to make a pizza.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Strong contractions.
My butterfly.
The baby is only five months along.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'крытие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'for the grand opening' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The grand opening is tomorrow.
Understand, Vitya, the opening is tomorrow.

examples.text: Я проверяю, всё ли готово к открытию.
examples.trans: I am checking whether everything is ready for the opening.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: Они хотели внести изменения в меню.
examples.trans: They wanted to make changes to the menu.
I meant well, understand.
I want coffee.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'соединиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to join'.

examples.trans: Would you not like to join us?

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и присоединиться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to join on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not even dare to say that.
Oh, you little macaque monkey!
Sorry, I thought the wrong thing.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everyone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do you have a conscience?
Everything's fine.
As you all know...

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guests' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a service for our guests.
Our hotel must surprise the guests.

examples.text: Гости ждут заказ с сегодняшнего дня.
examples.trans: Guests are waiting for orders starting today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'терять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will lose', paired with 'терять'.

examples.trans: We lost so much money today.
We will lose all our guests like this!
I've lost my key.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если хочешь их сохранить, не лезь!
examples.trans: If you want to keep them, stay out of my way!

examples.text: Если выиграю я, ты подчиняешься мне.
examples.trans: If I win, you obey me.
Come if you want.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'their', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They came yesterday and placed an order.

examples.text: Они хотели внести изменения в меню.
examples.trans: They wanted to make changes to the menu.
Were they here yesterday?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'охранить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to keep / preserve', paired with 'сохранять'.

examples.text: Если хочешь их сохранить, не лезь!
examples.trans: If you want to keep them, stay out of my way!

examples.text: А ты мою тайну вчера сохранил?
examples.trans: And did you keep my secret yesterday?
Save this document.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'poke nose, meddle', paired with 'полезть'.

examples.trans: I told you: stay away!

examples.text: Если хочешь их сохранить, не лезь!
examples.trans: If you want to keep them, stay out of my way!
Don't jump the queue!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'Lord', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Господи, да что же вы как дети?
examples.trans: Goodness, why are you acting like children?
Who is the master here now?
Applause, ladies and gentlemen!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Come on, everything is fine.
Come on, let's breathe.
Come on, that is all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'but, after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We are almost there already.
What is with you, mommy, huh?
Oh my God.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (polite/plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is with you, mommy, huh?

examples.text: Он ведёт себя как ревнивый парень.
examples.trans: He behaves like a jealous boyfriend.
You two argue really coolly.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'children' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The baby is only five months along.
This is my child.
The child is asleep.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: What is with you, mommy, huh?
I can't today.
That can't be.

meanings.en: to agree, to come to an arrangement
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'говориться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to reach an agreement', paired with 'договариваться'.

examples.trans: Cannot reach an agreement? Toss a coin.
It is time for you to finally reach a calm agreement!
We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'coin' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Cannot reach an agreement? Toss a coin.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть монетка.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always coin.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'toss / throw', paired with 'бросать'.

examples.trans: My wife has left me.
Throw the ball!

examples.text: Меня жена бросила. Два пальца сломаны.
examples.trans: My wife has left me. Two of my fingers are broken.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'it's time', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сейчас мы быстро наведём здесь порядок!
examples.trans: Right now we will quickly restore order here!
It is time for you to finally reach a calm agreement!

examples.text: С тех пор мы всегда вместе.
examples.trans: Since then we have always been together.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'конец').

examples.trans: It is time for you to finally reach a calm agreement!
Oh, it's warm at last!
We are finally home.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: It is time for you to finally reach a calm agreement!
Everything will be ready. Do not worry.
You'll do everything calmly.
